sections.title: Naming a risk, not a certainty
sections.content: *-hat/-het* has one more job beyond "can" and gentle suggestions: naming a possible bad outcome without predicting it as fact. *Ez veszélyes lehet* doesn't claim the thing definitely is dangerous — *lehet* (from *lenni* + *-het*) floats it as a real possibility, which is often exactly the caring, non-alarmist tone you want when warning someone about a *kockázat* (risk) or a *következmény* (consequence).

items.spanish: Ez a döntés komoly következményekkel járhat.
items.english: This decision could have serious consequences.

items.spanish: Ha most nem szólsz, később megbánhatod.
items.english: If you don't speak up now, you might regret it later.
Be careful, this could be dangerous!

sections.content: Pairing an *-hat/-het* warning with *vigyázz* ("watch out") or *nehogy* keeps the whole thing sounding like concern rather than a threat — you're pointing at a possible risk, not announcing doom, and the listener still gets to decide what to do about it.
